title: Component of the normalized integral presentation pullback square
statement: For every pro-etale test object W of U, the components at W of the two morphisms in the normalized integral presentation pullback square are equal.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Section 6.8; pointwise finite-quotient comparison

proof.text: At each residue level, compare the finite presentation map followed by continuous precomposition with the constant-sheaf direct-image map followed by the source finite presentation map. Sheafification extensionality reduces this to constant sections, on which finite_constants and the defining sheafification adjunct give equality.

The integral_residues equation identifies the presentation followed by the completed projection and finite comparison with the pointwise continuous reduction map. Conjugate continuous integral precomposition by the two integral presentation isomorphisms. The preceding finite square shows that this conjugate has precisely the defining finite projections of sfCompletedCoefficientMap; its existing uniqueness theorem identifies the maps.

Apply the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction to the desired square. Replace the completed direct-image map by the conjugated continuous precomposition just identified. Precompose with the target integral presentation isomorphism and cancel it. Evaluate both maps on a continuous integral section and a point. The integralInclusion_normalized, rationalInclusion_normalized and native pull_normalized equations make both values the same embedded integral function evaluated after the pullback projection.
Adjunction injectivity gives equality of the sheaf maps. Take their components at W to obtain the claimed ring-homomorphism equality; extensionality also covers empty test objects.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), Definition 6.8.1 and Section 6.8; constant-section normalization, finite-projection uniqueness and pointwise precomposition
